title: h-guard action rule
description: One action rule of a rule pack (rule pack schema 1), one rule per YAML file. Action rules check commands and file operations. Regular expressions are compiled and examples run by "h-guard config validate --rules <dir>", which is authoritative.

id.description: Rule id: lowercase letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-', starting with a letter or digit. A user rule with the id of a built-in rule replaces it (except locked rules). explicitly_requested and blast_radius are reserved.

enabled.description: Whether the rule is active; the config can override it (rules.<id>.enabled).

action.description: What a hit does: ask for confirmation or deny.

on.description: Action kinds the rule applies to.

locked.description: Hard rule whose content cannot be replaced. Only built-in rules can be locked.

requires_judge.description: The rule takes effect only when the judge is on; with the judge off its hits are only logged. Needs a question.

reason.description: Reason text shown to the user and the agent, by locale (en is required).

impact.description: Optional: what the operation would cause, shown after the reason when it interrupts, by locale (en is required when given).

advice.description: Optional: a safer way to continue, shown after the impact when it interrupts, by locale (en is required when given).

match.description: Local detection: match.exec for exec rules, match.file for file rules.

radius_floor.description: Lower bound of the blast radius (0..3) at which a hit stays dangerous; profiles can override it per rule.

bypassable_by_request.description: Whether an explicit request from the user can let a hit pass.

vetoable_by_judge.description: Whether a confident no from the judge can withdraw a local hit.

question.description: Question sent to the judge (in English). Only exec rules have questions.

examples.description: Examples checked by "h-guard config validate": hit must match, miss must not.

execMatch.description: Command regular expressions (case-insensitive), grouped by shell. Needs at least one pattern, or encoded. Patterns may use the file placeholders ({config}, {pi_agent_dir}, {dsh_home} and the others) outside character classes: each becomes the escaped directory, with / and \ as separators; an unset placeholder never matches.

command_position.description: Match only at command positions (required for deny rules).

strip_quotes.description: Blank out quoted text before matching.

redirects.description: Patterns matched against redirections, written as "command fd-operator target" (POSIX).

encoded.description: Also hit when encoded content is handed to an interpreter.

fileMatch.description: Path patterns for file actions. A pattern may start with {config}, {cache}, {extra_config}, {claude_config}, {codex_home}, {xdg_config}, {pi_agent_dir}, {omp_config} or {dsh_home}.

exclude.description: Paths that do not count as hits (matched literally).

example.description: A command example (shell and command) or a file example (one of the rule's file actions and path).
